newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC SAYS 1997 NET WILL EXCEED 1.7 BLN SFR.
newsitem.headline: SBC SAYS 1997 NET WILL EXCEED 1.7 BLN SFR.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) said it would "comfortably exceed" a 1997 net profit target of 1.7 billion Swiss francs despite an expected decline in results in the second half from a strong first half.
The forecast was more confident than earlier statements by Switzerland's third-biggest bank that it was confident of achieving the 1997 profit goal.
SBC said in a statement the full year's result would bring it closer to a medium-term goal of a 15 percent after-tax return on equity (ROE).

"Swiss Bank Corp does not expect results in the second half of the year to equal those in the first -- especially if financial markets fail to sustain their current high levels and transaction volumes fall," SBC said.

"The bank is, however, confident it will comfortably exceed its original target for 1997 of a net profit after tax and minorities of 1,700 million Swiss francs, bringing it an important step closer to its medium-term goal of an after-tax return on equity of 15 percent," it said.
In May, SBC chairman Georges Blum told shareholders he expected net profit to reach 1.7 billion Swiss francs for the full year 1997.
The bank's 1996 net was 606 million francs before extraordinaries and exceptional items, but a one-off charge for provisioning and restructuring knocked the result to a net loss of 1.955 billion.

All three of the big Swiss banks took extraordinary charges last year that left them with first-ever losses to settle a mounting backlog of bad domestic loans caused by six years of Swiss economic stagnation.
